## Description

In this assignment, you’ll create your own personal website using Quarto. **By the end of this assignment, you’ll have a website that you developed using data science tools.** You’ll also see how Quarto pages fit together like a puzzle to create a finished website.  

**Why make a website at all?** Having a website is a great way of developing a digital portfolio of your skills and interests. Read Elizabeth Pearson's [“4 Reasons Having a Personal Website Will Help Your Career”](https://www.forbes.com/sites/elizabethpearson/2024/08/28/4-reasons-having-a-personal-website-will-help-your-career/) for more.  

**How does making a website using Quarto actually work?** In class, we use Quarto markdown documents to write code with text, then render the document into the format we want (usually .pdf or .docx). One major benefit to using Quarto + Rprojects is that 1) Quarto renders to .html and 2) Quarto can render a bunch of Qmd files in a single project to create a website.  

**Why make a website using Quarto?** It’s a great way of demonstrating your skills to the data science community to show that you have some competency in knowing how Quarto documents work together.

## Requirements

Your website should have at least the following pages:

- [ ] a landing page with a
  - photo
  - brief bio (education, work, etc.)
- [ ] an about me page, which should include
  - at least 3 photos (can be of you or other things: pets, food, places)
  - at least 3 sections (of whatever you want to share about yourself)
- [ ] a project page (formatted as a blog) with
  - at least one post with code, its output, and writing about what you're doing and why
  - at least one post with a project or paper description (from a job, research project, class)  
- [ ] another page (a free for all)
  - could be about anything (hobbies, interests, etc.)
  - must be organized with section headers
  - must have photos or visuals of some kind
- [ ] a resume or CV
  - can be a page itself or a PDF
  
Additionally, you need to include all of the following add-ons/customizations:

- [ ] somewhere on your website, there should be an **interactive figure or map** (examples of how to do that [here](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1F5wKhd_8nX2x3dMvxZM5sE-pPPDgrQAKkFC4KGlE8jw/edit?usp=sharing))
- [ ] change the theme of your website from the default (here's a list of [Quarto themes](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-themes.html))
- [ ] change the CSS and/or SASS defaults for the theme to colors, fonts, etc. of your choice (here's a tutorial for [how to do that](https://ucsb-meds.github.io/customizing-quarto-websites/#/title-slide)).  

Lastly, you should double check that:  

- [ ] the text in your about me page, project page, and free for all page describing your activities/accomplishments is _new_ (i.e. you are not just copy-pasting bullet points and text from your resume)  

For your final submission (on Canvas), you will also submit a write-up of your process (details below).



## Workflow

### Part 1. Plan your website 

List the "pages" you want to include on your website with section headers.  

Plan your website in a word doc or in Google docs. _Do not code this_.  

For your project page, you could format using [blog posts](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-blog.html). You can enhance these with citations, figures, etc. to fill them out. Alternatively, you could use the blog post format to highlight classes you've taken to show you've developed skills in whatever those classes are about (for example, literary criticism, GIS, visual art). **Note:** you can have multiple pages in "blog" format - see [Sam Csik's personal website](https://samanthacsik.github.io/) where the "talks & workshops", "courses", "projects", and "posts" pages are all "blogs".  

Throughout your website, you could also have [photo galleries](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-lightbox-figures.html#galleries) to share any visual media you might have - illustration, photography, etc.  

:::{.callout-note title="Optional check-in here!"}
This check-in is _optional_. If you choose to do the check-in: remember that the more detail you have on your outline, the more thorough feedback you will receive.
:::

### Part 2. Make your website.

#### a. Create a new repository on GitHub and clone it to your computer.

On GitHub, create a new repository called `your-github-username.github.io`. For example, An's GitHub username is `an-bui`, so her repository name would be called `an-bui.github.io`.

Make sure you add a README when you are creating your repository.

Clone that repository to your computer.

#### b. Make R/Rstudio understand that this project is a website.

In the terminal, type:

```bash
quarto create-project --type website
```

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your Terminal window should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/01_create-project.png)
:::

#### c. Make some adjustments

These steps adjust some of the default rendering in Quarto.

1. Still in the terminal, type:

    ```bash
    touch .nojekyll
    ```

    This will disable some of the processing that Quarto will do for html files by default.

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your Terminal window should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/02_touch-nojekyll.png)
:::

2. Open the `_quarto.yml` file.

    At the top of this file, you should see a section that starts with `project:`.

    Make sure that all the rendered versions of `.qmd` files in your website go into a folder called `docs` by editing the `_quarto.yml`:

    ```bash
    project:
      type: website
      output-dir: docs
      
    # ~~ leave the other parts of the file as they are for now ~~
    ```

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your file should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/03_output-dir.png)
:::

#### d. Quit out of RStudio.

This step is to force the RStudio interface to provide a new tab in the top right of the window.

After you've quit out of RStudio, open it again with your website .Rproj file.

#### e. Render your website

After every change you make to any files in your website, you should render it.

In the top right corner, you should see a tab labelled **Build**.

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your RStudio window should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/04_build.png)
:::

Click the blue right arrow labelled **Render Website**.

You should see your website preview pop up in the Viewer pane (in the bottom right).

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your RStudio window should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/05_viewer.png)
:::

#### f. Stage, commit, and push your changes to the remote.

Do all of this in the Git tab.

#### g. Deploy your website using GitHub.

In your remote repo, navigate to Settings > Pages.

Be sure that **Branch** is set to `main` and the folder is set to `\docs`.

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your GitHub window should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/06_github-pages.png)
:::

Then, navigate back to the main page of your repo.

#### h. Find your deployment.

On the right hand side of the page, you should see a tab called Deployment.

Click on that link to find the URL for your website.

Note: you may see something along the lines of "Failed to deploy...". Don't worry about it! Wait for a few seconds, then refresh the page. You should see a new deployment pop up.

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your GitHub window should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/07_deployment.png)
:::

Click on your website url. Rejoice!

:::{.callout-tip title="Expand this to see what your website should look like" collapse="true"}
![](/assignments/images/quarto-website/08_website.png)
:::

#### i. Start changing things about your website

Now that you've gotten the basic parts down, you can start changing the appearance, pages, etc. on your website.

Follow [these directions](https://ucsb-meds.github.io/creating-quarto-websites/#change-stuff) written by Sam Shanny-Csik (from above!) to figure out what to change (and what to leave as is).

:::{.callout-note title="Required check-in here!"}
**For the required check-in, you should have all the pages created for your website** (landing page, about me page, project page, free for all page, resume/CV), but you do not have to have anything filled in yet.  
:::

### Part 3. Continue customizing your website.

Add content to each page following your outline from part 1.

### Part 4. Write about your process.

Respond to the following prompts with 1-3 sentences _each_:  

- What was hard about this? 
- What was easy?
- What was new to you?
- What was familiar to you?
- How did following the tutorial go for you?
- Which examples did you find most useful? Be specific about the components of your website that you copied from other people (e.g. I saw a photo gallery on this person's website, so I created a gallery of...).

## Checklist
Your submission should include  

- [ ] A link to the GitHub repository where your website is held  
- [ ] A link to your actual website  
- [ ] Your write up (as text in the Canvas submission)

Additionally, you should be committing and pushing changes throughout your completion of this assignment. Thus, you should make sure that you have **at least 10 commits/pushes with informative commit messages**.
